questions.title: Lunch Pack Business, Bread Options and Cellphone Sales Data

subQuestions.questionText:
Yvette runs a small business from home. She makes and sells lunch packs for learners. TABLE 1 shows items per lunch pack and cost prices: yoghurt is 6 per pack at R10,99; cost per yoghurt is R1,83.

Show how the cost of ONE yoghurt was calculated.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1 (RT): Reading correct values (R10,99 and 6) ✓
Mark 2 (MA): Dividing by 6 ✓

Calculation:
Cost of 1 yoghurt = $R10,99 \div 6$
                  = $R1,83$

Answer: $R1,83$

subQuestions.questionText: Apples cost R22,99 per bag and R2,87 per apple. Determine the maximum number of apples per bag.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1 (MA): Dividing correct values ✓
Mark 2 (A): Simplification ✓

Calculation:
Number of apples per bag = $R22,99 \div R2,87$
                        = $8,01$
                        = $8$ apples

Alternative accepted: $R22,99 \div 8 = R2,87$, therefore there are 8 apples.

Answer: $8$ apples

subQuestions.questionText:
The items in ONE lunch pack cost: fruit juice R5,63; sweets R3,54; apple R2,87; yoghurt R1,83; cheese R1,57; bread R1,55; fomo tray R1,37.

Show that the total cost to make ONE lunch pack is R18,36.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1 (RT): All correct values ✓
Mark 2 (M): Adding correct values ✓

Calculation:
Total cost = $R5,63 + R3,54 + R2,87 + R1,83 + R1,57 + R1,55 + R1,37$
           = $R18,36$

Answer: $R18,36$ ✓

subQuestions.questionText: The profit Yvette makes per lunch pack is R16,64. Calculate the selling price of ONE lunch pack.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1 (MA): Adding correct values ✓
Mark 2 (A): Simplification ✓

Calculation:
Selling price = Cost price + Profit
             = $R18,36 + R16,64$
             = $R35,00$

Answer: $R35,00$

subQuestions.questionText: Define the term profit in the given context.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1-2 (A): Difference between Selling Price and Cost Price ✓✓

Answer: Profit is the difference between the Selling price and the Cost price Yvette makes when selling the lunch packs.

Alternative accepted: Cover expenses and still able to make extra (= 2 marks).

subQuestions.questionText: Bulk price of 100% fruit juice = R135,00 (24 per box). Bulk price of sweets = R85,00 (24 per pack). Write down, as a simplified ratio, the bulk price of the 100% fruit juice to the bulk price of sweets.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1 (RT): Correct values ✓
Mark 2 (MA): Values in correct order ✓
Mark 3 (MCA): Simplification ✓

Calculation:
Ratio = $135 : 85$
      = $27 : 17$ (dividing both by 5)

Answer: $27 : 17$

Alternative (Unit Ratio = 3 marks):
$\dfrac{135}{85} : \dfrac{85}{85} = 1,588235294 : 1$

Note: MCA awarded if order is correct.

subQuestions.questionText:
Yvette's lunch pack has bread/bread roll options: White bread (W), brown bread (B) or a bread roll (R). The bread or bread roll can be toasted (T) or not toasted (N). A diagram shows the different options.

Name the type of diagram illustrated above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1-2 (A): Tree diagram ✓✓

Answer: Tree diagram

subQuestions.questionText: Complete missing labels (a) and (b) on the tree diagram. Label (a) is the missing main branch, and label (b) is the toasted outcome for bread roll.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1-2 (A): Correct option for (a) ✓✓
Mark 3-4 (A): Correct outcome for (b) ✓✓

Answers:
(a) Brown Bread
(b) RT (Bread Roll Toasted)

subQuestions.questionText: Write down the total number of outcomes (from the tree diagram).
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1-2 (A): Correct number ✓✓

Answer: $6$ outcomes

Reasoning: 3 bread types × 2 toasting options = 6 total outcomes (WT, WN, RT, RN, BT, BN).

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the number of toasted bread outcomes.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1-2 (A): Correct number ✓✓

Answer: $2$ toasted bread outcomes (WT and BT — only 'bread' counted, not bread roll)

Notes:
- If answer is 3 = 1/2 marks
- 3/6 = 0 marks
- 2/4 = 1/2 marks

subQuestions.questionText:
A company recorded the number of cellphones sold in two stores over 12 months. STORE A: 120, 350, 360, 220, 290, 160, 250, 210, 200, 310, 380, 380. STORE B: 180, 260, 440, 380, 180, 400, 230, 320, 420, 210, 170, 140. The diagrams below represent the data for each store.

Identify the type of diagram drawn above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1-2 (A): Correct name ✓✓

Answer: Box-and-whisker (plot/diagram)

subQuestions.questionText: Write out IQR in full.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1-2 (A): Correct explanation ✓✓

Answer: Inter-Quartile Range

Mark 1-2 (RT): Correct value ✓✓

Answer: $270$

Calculation (if needed):
Arranged: 120, 160, 200, 210, 220, 250, 290, 310, 350, 360, 380, 380
Median = $\dfrac{250 + 290}{2} = 270$

Notes:
- If calculated = 2 marks
- If the median of Store B (245) used = 1/2 marks

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the difference between the maximum and minimum value for Store B. (Store B data: 180, 260, 440, 380, 180, 400, 230, 320, 420, 210, 170, 140.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1 (RT): Correct value (440) ✓
Mark 2 (RT): Correct value (140) ✓
Mark 3 (CA): Simplification ✓

Calculation:
Difference = Max − Min
           = $440 - 140$
           = $300$

Answer: $300$

Notes:
- CA if one value is correct and subtracting
- Use Store A = 1/3 marks (CA)

questions.title: Levy Statement, VAT, and School Fees

subQuestions.questionText: Bongiwe received her levy statement of account from Rango Property Specialist for her rented unit. Use ANNEXURE A. Write down the reference number that Bongiwe must use when she pays her account.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1-2 (A): Correct reference number ✓✓ (AO – Answer Only)

Answer: BGD 0016

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE reason why reference numbers are used when making payments.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1-2 (A): Correct explanation ✓✓

Acceptable answers (any ONE):
- Easier to read numbers on long bank statements
- To identify which clients have made payments to their accounts
- Convenience
- Filing purposes

[Any reasonable identification/tracking-related answer is accepted.]

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the missing value A, which has been omitted from the statement. (Refer to ANNEXURE A.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1 (MA): Subtracting correct values ✓
Mark 2 (A): Simplification ✓

Calculation:
$A = R3\,205,51 - R3\,206,00 = -R0,49$
OR
$A = R1\,498,14 - R1\,498,63 = -R0,49$

Answer: $-R0,49$

Note: If a positive R0,49 is given = 1/2 marks

subQuestions.questionText: The total amount due for this invoice is R2 340,73, including 15% VAT. Calculate the total amount due, excluding VAT.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1 (MA): Multiplying by $\dfrac{100}{115}$ (or dividing by 1,15) ✓
Mark 2 (A): Simplification ✓

Calculation:
Amount excluding VAT = $R2\,340,73 \times \dfrac{100}{115}$
                    = $R2\,035,42$

OR
$R2\,340,73 \div 1,15 = R2\,035,42$

OR
VAT amount = $R2\,340,73 \times \dfrac{15}{115} = R305,31$
Amount excluding VAT = $R2\,340,73 - R305,31 = R2\,035,42$

Answer: $R2\,035,42$

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate (rounded to TWO decimal places) the standard levy for June 2021 as a percentage of the amount due on the statement.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1 (RT): Correct levy ✓
Mark 2 (RT): Correct denominator ✓
Mark 3 (CA): Simplification (CA if one value is correct) ✓
Mark 4 (R): Rounding ✓

Calculation:
Percentage = $\dfrac{R1\,498,63}{R2\,340,73} \times 100\%$
           = $64,02304378\%$
           = $64,02\%$

Answer: $64,02\%$

subQuestions.questionText: Write down a possible payment option Rango Property Specialist will accept.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1-2 (A): Correct option ✓✓

Acceptable answers (any ONE):
- All electronic bank payments
- All Bank Deposits
- Cheques
- EFT – card swipe
- Debit order
- Stop order
- Internal Transfer

[Any payment method shown on the statement/addendum is acceptable.]

subQuestions.questionText: Blueberry Gardens have 49 units in total. Calculate the total amount collected by the body corporate if all 49 units paid their levy CSOS on 1 July 2021. (CSOS levy = R30,90.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1 (RT): Identifying correct levy (R30,90) ✓
Mark 2 (MA): Multiplying correct values ✓
Mark 3 (CA): Simplification ✓

Calculation:
Total amount = $49 \times R30,90$
             = $R1\,514,10$

Answer: $R1\,514,10$

subQuestions.questionText: The Blueberry Gardens body corporate increased the standard levy by 6,45% from 1 August 2021. (Current standard levy = R1 498,63.) Calculate the new standard levy after the increase.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1 (MA): Correct value multiplied by 6,45% ✓
Mark 2 (CA): Simplification ✓
Mark 3 (MCA): Adding the increase ✓
Mark 4 (CA): Simplification ✓

Calculation:
Increase = $R1\,498,63 \times 6,45\% = R96,66$
New levy = $R1\,498,63 + R96,66 = R1\,595,29$

OR
$R1\,498,63 \times \dfrac{106,45}{100} = R1\,595,29$

Answer: $R1\,595,29$ (Accept $R1\,595,30$)

Note: Any other value from addendum × 6,45% = 3/4 marks

subQuestions.questionText:
Bongiwe has twins, Sandile and Sakhile, who attend a private school. The monthly transport cost is R929 (per child). The school year runs January to November (11 months).

Calculate the total transport cost for the twins for a full school year.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1 (MA): Multiplying R929,00 by 2 ✓
Mark 2 (MA): Multiplying by 11 ✓
Mark 3 (CA): Simplification ✓

Calculation:
Transport fee annually = $2 \times R929,00 \times 11$
                       = $R20\,438,00$

Answer: $R20\,438,00$

subQuestions.questionText:
Bongiwe intends on paying the school fees in full on 30 January.

Determine the total amount of money Bongiwe will spend in ONE school year for the twins to attend the private school, including aftercare and transport.

Details:
• Aftercare: R7 700 per school year per child
• 1st child's school fee: R30 723 per school year
• 10% discount on school fees for the second child
• 7,5% discount if school fees paid in full by 31 January
• Monthly transport cost: R929 per child
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1 (A): Aftercare fee ✓
Mark 2 (MA): Calculating discount ✓
Mark 3 (CA): Discounted School Fees by 10% ✓
Mark 4 (CA): Total fee ✓
Mark 5 (MA): Calculating 7,5% ✓
Mark 6 (CA): Discounted school fees ✓
Mark 7 (M): Adding all values ✓
Mark 8 (CA): Total spending ✓

CA from Question 2.2.1

Calculation:
Aftercare for 2 children: $R7\,700 \times 2 = R15\,400$

School fees for 2nd child with 10% discount:
$R30\,723 - R3\,072,30 = R27\,650,70$

Total school fees: $R30\,723 + R27\,650,70 = R58\,373,70$

Discount for paying early (7,5%):
$7,5\% \times R58\,373,70 = R4\,378,03$

School fees payable: $R58\,373,70 - R4\,378,03 = R53\,995,67$

Total spent by parent:
$R15\,400 + R53\,995,67 + R20\,438$
$= R89\,833,67$

Answer: $R89\,833,67$

Mark allocation breakdown:
- Aftercare: 1 mark
- 2nd learner fees: 2 marks
- Total fees - discount: 3 marks
- Adding and total: 2 marks

questions.title: Provincial Livestock Numbers and Agricultural Sector Sales

subQuestions.questionText:
TABLE 2 shows the estimated provincial half-yearly livestock numbers (in thousands) for the nine provinces in South Africa for August 2020 and February 2021.

Write down the province with the second highest number of sheep for February 2021.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1-2 (RT): Correct answer ✓✓

Answer: Northern Cape (NC)

Reasoning: From TABLE 2, sheep numbers Feb '21:
- Eastern Cape: 6 394
- Northern Cape: 5 079
- Free State: 4 362
- Western Cape: 2 497
The second highest is Northern Cape at 5 079 (thousand).

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate Eastern Cape's estimated total number of livestock for August 2020. (Cattle = 3 050; Sheep = 6 513; Goats = 1 991 — all in thousands.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1 (RT): Correctly estimated values ✓
Mark 2 (MA): Adding values ✓
Mark 3 (CA): Answer in correct format ✓

Calculation:
Total = $(3\,050 + 6\,513 + 1\,991)$ thousands
      = $11\,554\,000$

Answer: $11\,554\,000$

Notes:
- CA two correct values in thousands
- Penalty for omitting thousands = 2/3 marks
- AO 11 554 = 2/3 marks

subQuestions.questionText:
The provincial mean number of sheep is 2 400 444. A farmer in Limpopo stated that the missing value A in the table is less than 200 (in thousands). Verify, showing ALL calculations, whether the farmer's statement is valid.

(Sheep values in thousands for Aug '20: WC 2 545; NC 5 182; FS 4 330; EC 6 513; KZN 628; MP 1 527; LP A; GT 84; NW 596.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1 (M): Concept of mean ✓
Mark 2 (C): Converting to table values ✓
Mark 3 (A): Adding table values ✓
Mark 4 (MA): Multiplying by 9 ✓
Mark 5 (MCA): Simplification ✓
Mark 6 (CA): Simplification ✓
Mark 7 (O): Conclusion ✓

Calculation:
Mean = $\dfrac{\text{Sum of all values}}{9}$

$2\,400,444 = \dfrac{2\,545 + 5\,182 + 4\,330 + 6\,513 + 628 + 1\,527 + A + 84 + 596}{9}$

$A + 21\,405 = 2\,400,444 \times 9$
$A = 21\,603,996 - 21\,405$
$A = 198,996$

Since $198,996 < 200$, the farmer's assumption is VALID. ✓

Alternative method:
$2\,400\,444 \times 9 = 21\,603\,996 = 21\,603,996$ thousand
$A = 21\,603,996 - (2\,545 + 5\,182 + 4\,330 + 6\,513 + 628 + 1\,527 + 84 + 596)$
$A = 21\,603,996 - 21\,405 = 198,996$
Farmer's statement is VALID.

subQuestions.questionText: South Africa's agricultural sector sales in 2019 amounted to R317,6 billion. ANNEXURE B shows the distribution of these sales. State whether the data displayed on ANNEXURE B is categorical or numerical data.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1-2 (A): Correct answer ✓✓

Answer: Numerical data

Reasoning: The data on ANNEXURE B contains numerical values (percentages and rand amounts), making it numerical data.

subQuestions.questionText: Determine missing value A. (From ANNEXURE B: Total = 25%; other values = 5%, 2%, and 2%.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1 (MA): Subtracting correct value ✓
Mark 2 (CA): Simplification ✓ (AO – Answer Only)

Calculation:
$A = 25\% - (5 + 2 + 2)\%$
$A = 25\% - 9\%$
$A = 16\%$

Answer: $16\%$

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate, in millions, the actual rand value of horticulture sales. (Horticulture = 27% of R317,6 billion.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1 (MA): Calculating % ✓
Mark 2 (CA): Simplification ✓
Mark 3 (C): Converting to million ✓

Calculation:
Horticulture = $27\% \times R317,6$ billion
             = $R85,752$ billion
             = $R85\,752$ million

Answer: $R85\,752$ million

subQuestions.questionText: Give a valid reason why there is a category for other livestock under animals.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1-2 (A): Correct answer ✓✓

Acceptable answers (any ONE):
- South Africa has other livestock like goats and pigs whose percentage is very small
- Any other poultry that the percentage is too small
- The smaller categories are grouped together as their individual percentages are too small to display separately

[Any reasonable answer linking 'other' to grouping small percentages is accepted.]

questions.title: Orange Juice Prices and Water Tariffs

subQuestions.questionText: The average monthly retail price for orange juice per litre in Canadian dollars (CAD) for 2018 to 2021 is shown on the ANSWER SHEET. Calculate (in CAD) the difference between the price of orange juice in January 2019 and in February 2019.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1 (RT): Correct values ✓
Mark 2 (M): Subtracting ✓
Mark 3 (A): Simplification ✓

Calculation:
February 2019: CAD 4,10
January 2019: CAD 4,30
Difference: $CAD\,4,30 - CAD\,4,10 = CAD\,0,20$

Answer: February 2019 cost CAD 0,20 less than January 2019

subQuestions.questionText: Write down the month and year in which the price of orange juice was at its lowest. (Refer to graph on ANSWER SHEET.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1 (RT): Correct month ✓
Mark 2 (RT): Correct year ✓

Answer: February 2018 (or 02/2018)

subQuestions.questionText: State the month and years in which the price of orange juice was exactly the same. (Refer to graph on ANSWER SHEET.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1 (RT): Correct month ✓
Mark 2 (RT): Correct years ✓

Answer: November 2018 and November 2019 (or 11/2018 and 11/2019)

Alternative accepted answers (1/2 marks each):
1) Sept 2018 and Oct 2019
2) Nov 2020 and Dec 2018
3) Jan 2019 and Aug 2020

subQuestions.questionText: Determine the median monthly price of orange juice for 2020. (2020 monthly values in CAD: 4,35; 4,39; 4,23; 4,27; 4,43; 4,32; 4,26; 4,3; 4,13; 4,06; 4,143; 4,24.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1 (A): Arranging in order ✓
Mark 2 (RT): Correctly identifying middle values ✓
Mark 3 (M): Concept of median (÷2) ✓
Mark 4 (A): Simplification ✓

Calculation:
Arranged: 4,06 | 4,13 | 4,143 | 4,23 | 4,24 | 4,26 | 4,27 | 4,3 | 4,32 | 4,35 | 4,39 | 4,43

Middle two values: 4,26 and 4,27

Median = $\dfrac{4,26 + 4,27}{2} = \dfrac{8,53}{2} = CAD\,4,265$

subQuestions.questionText: Describe the trend of the price of orange juice from February 2018 to July 2018.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1 (A): Increase ✓
Mark 2 (A): Indicate decrease ✓

Answer: The price increases steadily until it reaches June, thereafter it decreases slightly.

Accepted alternatives:
- Steadily increasing to June then decline in July month = full marks
- Upward trend and downward trend = 1/2 marks

subQuestions.questionText:
An analyst predicted that the price of orange juice would drop by 0,16 CAD from February 2021 to March 2021. Determine the year-on-year percentage increase from March 2020 to March 2021. (February 2021 price = CAD 4,46; March 2020 price = CAD 4,23.)

You may use the following formula: $\text{Percentage Increase} = \dfrac{\text{New value} - \text{Old value}}{\text{Old value}} \times 100\%$
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1 (A): Finding price of March 2021 ✓
Mark 2 (MCA): Substituting new value ✓
Mark 3 (A): Substituting old value ✓
Mark 4 (A): Denominator ✓
Mark 5 (CA): Simplification ✓

Calculation:
Price for March 2021 = $CAD\,4,46 - CAD\,0,16 = CAD\,4,30$

Percentage Increase = $\dfrac{4,30 - 4,23}{4,23} \times 100\%$
                    = $\dfrac{0,07}{4,23} \times 100\%$
                    = $1,65\%$

Answer: $1,65\%$

Notes:
- No penalty for missing unit
- Candidates left out % sign awarded full marks
- Percentage symbol included in 'percentage increase'

subQuestions.questionText:
John considers moving from Toronto in Canada to either Cape Town or Ekurhuleni in South Africa. ANNEXURE C shows water tariffs. John estimates 45 kℓ of water per month.

John states that if he chooses to live in Cape Town, he will be paying R3 600 more per year compared to a person living in Ekurhuleni who also uses an average of 45 kℓ of water per month.

Show, by means of calculations, whether John's statement is CORRECT.

(Cape Town tariffs: Fixed monthly R104,50; Step 1: 6 kℓ × R15,10; Step 2: 4,5 kℓ × R20,75; Step 3: 24,5 kℓ × R28,20; Step 4: 10 kℓ × R52,04.
Ekurhuleni tariffs: Fixed monthly R0,00; Step 1: 6 kℓ × R13,50; Step 2: 9 kℓ × R22,24; Step 3: 15 kℓ × R27,24; Step 4: 15 kℓ × R33,90.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1 (RT): Fixed monthly (Cape Town) ✓
Mark 2 (RT): Using correct values (Cape Town) ✓
Mark 3 (S): Calculating tariffs (Cape Town) ✓
Mark 4 (CA): Finding total cost (Cape Town) ✓
Mark 5 (RT): Using correct values (Ekurhuleni) ✓
Mark 6 (S): Calculating tariffs (Ekurhuleni) ✓
Mark 7 (CA): Finding total cost (Ekurhuleni) ✓
Mark 8 (MCA): Finding monthly difference ✓
Mark 9 (MCA): Finding yearly difference ✓
Mark 10 (O): Correct conclusion ✓

Calculation:

CAPE TOWN:
Fixed Monthly = $R104,50$
$6$ kℓ × $R15,10$ = $R90,60$
$4,5$ kℓ × $R20,75$ = $R93,38$
$24,5$ kℓ × $R28,20$ = $R690,90$
$10$ kℓ × $R52,04$ = $R520,40$
Total = $R1\,499,78$

EKURHULENI:
Fixed Monthly = $R0,00$
$6$ kℓ × $R13,50$ = $R81,00$
$9$ kℓ × $R22,24$ = $R200,16$
$15$ kℓ × $R27,24$ = $R408,60$
$15$ kℓ × $R33,90$ = $R508,50$
Total = $R1\,198,26$

Difference per month: $R1\,499,78 - R1\,198,26 = R301,52$
Difference per year: $R301,52 \times 12 = R3\,618,24$

Conclusion: He is INCORRECT. The actual annual difference is R3 618,24, not R3 600 (a difference of R18,24).

questions.title: Pension Fund, Tax, Loan and International Currency

subQuestions.questionText: Shamila, a teacher at a local high school, is going on retirement. The estimated value of her full pension fund benefit is R3 457 920,00. Write out Shamila's full pension fund benefit in words.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1-2 (A): Correct answer ✓✓

Answer: Three million, four hundred and fifty seven thousand, nine hundred and twenty rand.

subQuestions.questionText: Shamila has two options. Option 1: Withdraw a third of the full pension fund benefit. Determine the amount of money that Shamila can withdraw if she chooses Option 1.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1 (MA): Multiplying by fraction ✓
Mark 2 (A): Simplification ✓ (AO – Answer Only)

Calculation:
$\dfrac{1}{3}$ withdrawal = $\dfrac{1}{3} \times R3\,457\,920$
                          = $R1\,152\,640$

Answer: $R1\,152\,640$

subQuestions.label: 5.1.3(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
Shamila decides to choose Option 2 (withdraw 100%) as she wants to loan money to her daughter. Shamila states that the amount of tax she will pay on the estimated value of her pension fund of R3 457 920,00 is more than R1 000 000.

Using TABLE 4 (Retirement Benefit Tax Table 1 March 2021 to 28 February 2022): For taxable income above R1 050 000, tax is R130 500 + 36% of taxable income above R1 050 000.

Verify, showing ALL calculations, whether her statement is CORRECT.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1 (A): Correct tax bracket ✓
Mark 2 (SF): Correct substitution ✓
Mark 3 (S): Simplification ✓
Mark 4 (MCA): Simplification ✓
Mark 5 (CA): Simplification ✓
Mark 6 (O): Conclusion ✓

Calculation:
Tax bracket: $R130\,500 + 36\%$ of taxable income above $R1\,050\,000$

Tax = $R130\,500 + 36\% \times (R3\,457\,920,00 - R1\,050\,000,00)$
    = $R130\,500 + (36\% \times R2\,407\,920)$
    = $R130\,500 + R866\,851,20$
    = $R997\,351,20$

Conclusion: Her statement is NOT correct. The actual tax (R997 351,20) is LESS than R1 000 000.

subQuestions.label: 5.1.3(b)
subQuestions.questionText: The ratio of the estimated value of Shamila's full pension (before tax) to her daughter's loan amount is 9,8798 : 1. Determine, to the nearest thousand rand, the amount that her daughter will borrow.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1 (A): Using correct values ✓
Mark 2 (MA): Dividing by 9,8798 ✓
Mark 3 (CA): Simplification ✓
Mark 4 (R): Rounded to nearest 1 000 ✓

Calculation:
Loan amount = $R3\,457\,920,00 \div 9,8798$
            = $R349\,998,99$
            = $R350\,000,00$

OR
Let Loan amount = L
$\dfrac{9,8798}{1} = \dfrac{3\,457\,920}{L}$
$L = \dfrac{3\,457\,920}{9,8798}$
$L = R349\,998,99 \approx R350\,000,00$

Answer: $R350\,000,00$ (or R350 thousand)

subQuestions.label: 5.1.3(c)
subQuestions.questionText: Suraya agrees to borrow the money at a simple interest rate of 7,8% per annum. She intends to repay the total amount with interest at the end of a three-year period. Determine the total amount she will have to repay after three years.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1 (MA): Multiply by % and 3 ✓
Mark 2 (MCA): Simplification (at least two correct values) ✓
Mark 3 (MCA): Adding values ✓
Mark 4 (CA): Simplification ✓

CA from Question 5.1.3(b)

Calculation:
Total interest = $R350\,000 \times \dfrac{7,8}{100} \times 3$
               = $R81\,900$

Total amount = Loan + Interest
             = $R81\,900 + R350\,000$
             = $R431\,900$

Answer: $R431\,900$

subQuestions.questionText:
Suraya has established that the cost of relocating a family of four to New Zealand is approximately R280 000. A skilled migrant resident visa costs €2 093 and a visa for entrepreneurs costs NZ$4 745. TABLE 5 shows exchange rates on 3 September 2021: 1 ZAR = €0,0581765; 1 ZAR = NZ$0,0969907.

Determine the exchange rate of the New Zealand dollar (NZ$) in terms of the euro (€) on 3 September 2021 in the form 1 NZD : ...
subQuestions.memoText:

Calculation:
$0,0969907$ NZD = $1$ ZAR
$0,0581765$ € = $1$ ZAR

Therefore: $0,0969907$ NZD = $0,0581765$ €
Dividing both sides by $0,0969907$:
$\dfrac{0,0969907}{0,0969907}$ NZD = $\dfrac{0,0581765}{0,0969907}$ €

$1$ NZD = $0,59981524$ €

Answer: $1$ NZD : $0,5998152$ € (approximately $1$ NZD : $0,60$ €)
